perspective:
Harold Padilla’s available information is limited to what he personally did, observed, felt, and was told:

- He is a Project Manager and has a friendship/professional relationship with Arthur Begum, a police officer he trusts for advice.
- He felt frustrated and anxious because he believed his project team was unmotivated and that this was hurting project progress.
- He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- He told Arthur the team seemed unmotivated and that he was at his wit’s end.
- He heard Arthur advise him to understand each team member’s individual motivation, make people feel valued/understood, and have one-on-one conversations.
- He admitted to Arthur that he had focused mostly on project goals/deadlines rather than personal motivations. He said he would try Arthur’s suggestion and felt hopeful.
- He told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand their motivations, believing this would help them work better together. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. He planned to schedule those meetings.
- After trying the advice, he observed that the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried, and told Arthur this.
- He heard Arthur suggest there might be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that he should dig deeper.
- He set up another round of one-on-one meetings and asked team members about concerns/problems.
- He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension among a few team members affecting work.
- He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- He told them he would look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, and that their well-being was important.
- He told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that their concerns were being addressed.
- He said he was glad and that their input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.

He does not have access to private thoughts, hidden motives, or information beyond what was stated in these interactions and what he personally observed or felt.
